#114541. Preserving Henry Ford’s failed Amazonian empire

Preserving Henry Ford’s failed Amazonian empire

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1222 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theartnewspaper

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Deep in the Amazon Rainforest, in the Brazilian state of Pará, lies the dilapidated settlement of Fordlândia.
  • Earlier this year, almost a century after Fordlândia was built, a federal court ruled that it must be protected as a heritage site under the Brazilian constitution.
  • Ford’s firm originally acquired the land for what would become Fordlândia in 1927.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Deep in the Amazon Rainforest, in the Brazilian state of Pará, lies the dilapidated settlement of Fordlândia. A once bustling—albeit highly exploitative—village, it was established by the US industrialist Henry Ford in the 1920s. Fordlândia’s sole purpose was to serve as a rubber-tapping enterprise that would provide materials for the Ford Motor Tech giant. But less than a decade after its founding, the rubber crops failed. With the development of synthetic rubber following close behind, Ford abandoned the project in 1945, and the village along the Tapajós River fell into severe disrepair.

Earlier this year, almost a century after Fordlândia was built, a federal court ruled that it must be protected as a heritage site under the Brazilian constitution. Local and national authorities have until the end of this month to come up with a conservation plan.

Ford’s firm originally acquired the land for what would become Fordlândia in 1927. He envisioned building a Midwestern-style village as a hub for latex extraction, supplying materials for his factories in Michigan. Ford hoped to upend the dominance of British-controlled rubber plantations in Southeast Asia, which had left US manufacturers dependent on foreign suppliers.

Recent findings suggest that fordlândia, beyond giving the Ford Motor Company control over its supply of raw materials, was imagined as a self-sufficient settlement for around 10,000 people in the Amazon. Ford himself viewed Fordlândia as a sociological experiment intended to “Americanise” the local population, although the tycoon never visited his dystopian village. Workers there, many of them Indigenous people and migrants from northeastern Brazil, endured cultural subjugation and often faced dangerous conditions—including having to work through the hottest part of the day. Hundreds of people died during the short-lived project.

Workers organised a mutiny in 1930 after unreasonable restrictions were imposed in Fordlândia, including the prohibition of alcohol and tobacco, as well as the requirement of US customs like square dancing and a diet of wholewheat bread, brown rice, oatmeal and canned peaches. Shortly afterwards there was a full-scale riot, in which workers chased their American managers and the village cook into the jungle. The Brazilian army was brought in to restore order. The organization subsequently fired a number of workers and appointed a new manager to complete Fordlândia’s infrastructure. (An agreement on serving different food to the workers was also reached.).

Fordlândia Dance Hall, around 1933 The Collections of the Henry Ford.

In a recent development, ford’s social experiment unfolded alongside agricultural problems. Without the consultation of local experts, the rubber trees had been planted too close together. This made them vulnerable to disease and pests, and the growing conditions along the river were unsuitable. In 1933, at the recommendation of the American plant pathologist James Robert Weir, a second plantation was established downstream at Belterra, where conditions were more appropriate. Although it fared better than Fordlândia, production remained costly and it never became commercially viable.

Sources indicate that no usable latex was ever produced in Fordlândia. After investing millions of dollars with no return, Ford sold the land back to the Brazilian government. The population dropped by more than 90% in the following years, but squatters and families moved back into the decaying structures in the 2000s. Around 3,000 people live in Fordlândia today, even as the village remains unconnected to paved roads.

Recent findings suggest that the federal process for the designation of Fordlândia as a heritage site has been unresolved since the 1990s, when the move was first suggested by local advocates. In 2015, Brazil’s federal public prosecutor’s office filed a lawsuit stating that the site had “unquestionable” cultural value. In 2024, the National Institute of Historic and Artistic Heritage (Iphan) countered that Fordlândia lacked the criteria required for federal heritage listing, pointing to the loss of its original characteristics and the site’s deteriorated condition.

It has been revealed that but in May 2026 a federal court ruled that, even without formal heritage status, the site should be protected. This decision was based on a 1988 constitutional article that mandates the conservation of both material and immaterial assets connected to Brazilian communities. The court added that uncertainty over ownership of the site had been used repeatedly as justification for inaction, and that the state of Pará and the municipality of Aveiro (which administers Fordlândia) had previously signed an agreement to begin conservation measures that never materialised. It also alleged that some interventions had been carried out without authorisation.

A Fordlândia sawmill in 1931, before the Ford Motor Firm’s rubber-plantation project was halted The Collections of the Henry Ford.

It has been revealed that the court ruled that Iphan must now work with the state and municipality to deliver a plan by the end of November 2026, outlining the responsibilities of each government entity and the needs of each site in Fordlândia—including emergency measures for structures at imminent risk. Once approved, conservation work must begin within 30 days. If deadlines are not met, the court will impose a daily fine of $2,000 (10,000 reais) on the federal government and Iphan, and a $1,000 (5,000 reais) fine on the state and municipality. Iphan must also begin the administrative process to recognise Fordlândia as a heritage site.

According to recent reports, in a statement to The Art Newspaper, a spokesperson for Iphan says the agency does not comment on ongoing legal proceedings. It remains unclear if Iphan aims to counter the court’s decision. “In May 2024, Iphan’s cultural-heritage advisory council denied Fordlândia’s designation as Brazilian cultural heritage,” the spokesperson says. “Iphan reiterates that it remains committed to the preservation of Brazilian cultural heritage, as mandated by the constitution.”.

The sites to be reviewed include the former Fordlândia Hospital, designed by the Detroit architect Albert Kahn; the long-abandoned industrial and port warehouses; the houses of the American Village, where the firm’s American managers lived; the workers’ village; the Henry Ford School; the Cine Patinha, a cinema whose roof has recently collapsed; and a convent on a cliff overlooking the Tapajós River, built in the post-Ford era and active until the early 2010s. All these structures have been exposed to the Amazon’s heat, humidity and heavy rainfall for years.

According to recent reports, fordlândia remains highly remote, receiving few outside visitors and requiring a minimum six-hour trip to reach via high-speed boat. Still, there is evidence that intrepid travellers have made the journey. A tech giant specialising in tours of the Amazon is presently offering a five-day visit to the region, including a stop in Fordlândia, for approximately $3,000 (16,000 reais) per person. Reviews for “Fordlândia Ghost Town” on TripAdvisor average 4.7 out of 5 stars, with one reviewer in 2016 calling the site “historical, magical and melancholic”, and another saying it tells a story of “hubris, determination, paternalism and ultimately failure”.

According to recent reports, although Fordlândia is unlikely to be commercialised as a tourist destination, the village’s surviving infrastructure has come to represent an unusual and failed attempt to Americanise and industrialise the Amazon. The remnants of the settlement also tell the story of the Brazilian workers who lived there, and those who have continued to inhabit it. The Brazilian government maintains that Fordlândia has “unquestionable historical, cultural and architectural value”, and that it represents “an American attempt to break the British monopoly on rubber and bring modern infrastructure to the middle of the Amazon”.

Liene PixCut S1 review: This sticker printer is better than Cricut's StickerPix, and here's why

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2266 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Creativebloq

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Liene PixCut S1 is expensive, but its excellent prints, clever templates and fuss-free batch production make it a better dedicated sticker printer than Cricut's StickerPix, and running costs are slightly cheaper.
  • Quality prints, with rich colours and sharp detail.
  • Clever 'Phone Back' feature for custom phone decals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Liene PixCut S1 is expensive, but its excellent prints, clever templates and fuss-free batch production make it a better dedicated sticker printer than Cricut's StickerPix, and running costs are slightly cheaper.

Laminates and cuts stickers in one simple process.

Quality prints, with rich colours and sharp detail.

10,000+ templates and 50,000 graphics to use.

Clever 'Phone Back' feature for custom phone decals.

Some app templates are frustrating to edit.

Why you can trust Creative Bloq Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.

Price: $279.99 (Starter Kit), $346.99 (Inspire Kit); £379.99 (Bundle).

Print tech: Four-layer dye-sublimation thermal transfer (D2T2), with a laminate pass.

Resolution: 300 × 300 dpi, 256 shades per colour.

Sticker size: 4 x 7in; printable area 3.9 x 6.7in.

Photo size: 4 x 6in; printable area 3.94 × 5.83in.

Cutting: Single axis, up to 2ips; fine-point carbide blade, 45-degree angle, 1.0mm tip.

Capacity: 36-sheet paper cassette; ribbon cartridge covers 36 sheets of 4 x 7in.

App support: iOS 9.0+ and Android 4.1+.

Dimensions: 281 x 196 x 104.5mm.

In the box: Printer, paper cassette, 18 sheets each of sticker and photo paper, ink cartridge, blade, power adaptor, manual.

The Liene PixCut S1 prints, laminates and cuts stickers in one go, straight from your phone. It costs between $280 and $347 in the US depending on the bundle (around £349 to £380 in the UK), and it only does a relatively narrow range of things. But it does them very well, and I prefer it to Cricut's StickerPix Print + Cut, even though the PixCut S1 costs around £100 more.

That distinction becomes more key when you start making several sheets. The PixCut S1 is designed to get a job ready, print it, laminate it and cut it, without having to think too much about the process. It's a specialist machine with an approachable app, and that's actually its biggest strength.

It measures 281 x 196 x 104.5mm and weighs 2.9kg, so it sits on my craft table without taking over and is light enough to shift onto a shelf when you're done. You'll need a bit of clear space at each end for the paper to feed through. Setup is quick. The booklet has clear diagrams for removing the packaging and fitting the cartridge, and the paper tray clicks easily onto the back. Then scan the QR code, install the app, verify your email and pair over Bluetooth. It can pair with up to three devices, which is handy if more than one person in the house wants to use it, or if, like me, you tend to spend the day moving from phone to laptop to tablet without ever settling.

My review unit shipped with a US plug adaptor, so if you're buying in the UK, check what's in the box, but assume, as this is a US-based manufacturer, that you will need to pick up a plug adapter (luckily I review the best drawing tablets, so I have a drawer of adapters).

Industry observers note that the PixCut S1 uses four-layer thermal dye sublimation: it lays down colour in passes, then seals it with a protective laminate layer. It prints at 300 x 300 dpi with 256 tones per colour, delivering a smooth, continuous finish rather than the dotty look of inkjet.

There's no liquid ink here. The cartridge holds dye film, so swapping it is clean and quick, and each one lasts about 36 sheets. It prints stickers on 4 x 7 inch sheets (roughly 3.9 x 6.7 in printable) and photos on 4 x 6 inches. That's the limit of what it can make, so think small stickers, labels, tags and prints rather than big projects.

Printing times vary from about one to two minutes per sticker sheet, depending on the design complexity. It's quite mesmerising to watch the little printer layer yellow, magenta, and cyan dye as it feeds the design in and out of the printing slot. Looking at the app, you can see each layer scrub down in real time, which is a nice touch.

According to recent reports, the paper tray and cartridge each hold about 36 sheets, so you can work through a decent batch without constantly stopping to replenish supplies. You don't have to print a design, export it, move it into another piece of software, and then set up a separate cutting job. Everything happens in one machine, which makes PixCut S1 feel like what it is: a mini-printer that makes stickers and prints, not a craft machine that wants to do more.

I found the workflow dependable and, importantly, repeatable. Once you've got your design sorted, you can send another sheet through without rethinking the process. That's useful if you're making a set of labels for a small business, preparing gift stickers for Christmas or producing several sheets of your own artwork. It isn't a machine for huge commercial runs, but for short batches it makes a lot of sense.

Speaking of the app, it's incredibly easy to use. If you've used a Cricut and Design Space, you'll know that designing and prepping a job can be a project in itself. Liene's app avoids that because it only has to drive one machine, not a whole ecosystem of craft cutters, printers and heat presses. The Canvas section lets you search templates – type 'boats', and you get a selection – or browse categories like Christmas, holidays and decorative stickers. Pick one, edit it, add your own images and text, and you're away.

Industry observers note that the modes are Stickers, Labels, Phone Back, Cards and Invites, and Photos. They all follow the same workflow, so learning one means you've learned the lot, which again plays into the streamlined nature of using the PixCut S1.

There are 10,000+ templates and 50,000 graphics to use, which is a lot, but they're easy to categorise and search.

It has been revealed that stickers are the mode I've been using most during this review because they're so fun and useful. Choose a style (Original, Watercolour or Comic Crew), upload a photo, and the app generates six sticker designs from it. Edit them on the canvas, delete some to make a bigger sticker, or add text and shapes. Hit Make It, load the paper the app asks for, and press Cut.

Labels come with many ready-made designs: pantry, living spaces, medicine, business, names, plus office, planner and bath collections. They're all editable, which makes them handy for home organising or a small business.

In a recent development, phone Back stood out to me, and I created a number of fun decals, including a Christmas-illustrated pattern from my own photos. It's simple: pick your phone and model from the Apple, Samsung, Motorola and Google ranges, then use a template or build your own with photos, text, shapes and lines. The PixCut S1 prints it, coats it and cuts it to fit your exact model. I haven't seen anything quite like this on other machines, and it reveals what a combined printer and cutter can do that separate devices can't. (You could do something similar on Cricut, but you'll need to measure and design the templates yourself.).

It has been revealed that the Photos section covers standard prints, AI portraits, ID photos and collages of up to nine images. The ID photo tool is useful, with on-screen guides to help you frame yourself. The poster option is weaker. Some templates add text I couldn't work out how to edit, which is annoying in an app that is otherwise so flexible.

Photo prints are where the PixCut S1 excels. With 300dpi and 256 tones per colour, you get rich colour and sharp detail, far better than I'd expect from a machine this size. As we're getting overloaded with images, I'm reassured that I can create professional-looking prints from my camera roll at the touch of a button. I tried it with some of my digital art too, and the results were excellent, making professional-quality postcards.

One area where it will excel over the holidays (or for birthdays and events) is cards and gift tags. Cards print on sticker paper and are cut into rectangles, so you can peel and stick them onto a card. Tags are better because you can edit each one separately and print a single tag for one person instead of wasting a full sheet.

Industry observers note that the other significant difference between the Liene and Cricut is the cost of keeping them fed. The PixCut S1 isn't cheap to buy, but the running costs are more reasonable than you might expect for a dedicated sticker printer. My review bundle includes one cartridge, 18 sheets of sticker paper and 18 sheets of photo paper – similar to the PixCut S1 deal on Amazon. A refill pack with two cartridges and 72 sheets is around £39.99 on Amazon, which works out at roughly 55p per sheet.

Recent findings suggest that remember that each cartridge is rated for around 36 sheets, so you're getting 72 prints from the two cartridges and 72 sheets of paper in a refill bundle. You also can't buy a mixed sticker-and-photo pack, so you'll need to decide which material you'll use most.

Only Liene's paper works, so it's not a completely open system, and you're limited to 4 x 7 in sticker and 4 x 6 in photo sheets, so you don't get the material variety you would with a Cricut. But the cost per sheet is reasonable for a laminated, cut-to-shape sticker, especially when you fill a sheet with several designs rather than making a single small sticker.

In a recent development, cricut's StickerPix Print + Cut has a similar restriction around its own paper and cartridges, and its $299.99 / £249.99 price makes it cheaper to buy initially, but its refills cost more at $47.99 / £47.99. But the lower entry price doesn't necessarily make it better value if you'll use it regularly. You're still buying dedicated consumables, and you're also buying into Design Space.

Sources indicate that there's another practical difference when you're making multiple copies. When I used the Cricut, I found that finished sheets need to be manually cleared from the cutting area before the next one can start. It's hardly a deal-breaker, but it adds another little intervention to what should be a simple print-and-cut process. The Liene's appeal is that it feels more like feeding a printer than operating a craft machine.

Sources indicate that but oddly, the limitations of the PixCut S1 play into its favour. It's a precise, small and relatively fast device made for one thing – printing and cutting stickers. You're not overburdened with options and can focus on making great prints. Within this narrow category, the PixCut S1 excels and offers options Cricut doesn't, like iPhone case decals. You can create your own templates in Cricut Design Space and fiddle around, but the PixCut S1 does it out of the box for every iPhone (and most Androids).

Here's an at-a-glance look at Liene versus Cricut, because the difference is wafer-thin, but for me, the Pixcut S1 just edges it on running costs and its narrow but specialist nature – especially when it comes to everyday uses like quick phone stickers.

Sources indicate that prints, laminates and cuts stickers in one pass from your phone, using a dedicated app with 10,000+ templates and built-in Phone Back decals. Four-layer dye-sublimation at 300dpi gives rich, sharp prints. It's limited to two paper sizes and Liene consumables, with refills around 55p a sheet.

It has been revealed that A cheaper way into print-and-cut stickers, but it runs through Cricut's Design Space app and ecosystem. Refills cost more (£47.99 for 72 prints), it's tied to Cricut's own paper and cartridges, and phone decals mean designing your own templates.

It has been revealed that if you only make stickers occasionally, this is a lot of money for a specialist machine. And if you're mainly after ordinary 6 x 4 inch photo prints, there are cheaper ways to get them. But if you regularly make stickers, labels, phone backs, tags and photo prints – and will make good use of the thousands of templates – it's an easy recommendation.

Industry observers note that it won't replace a full craft cutter, and it isn't intended to, but as a focused machine for making stickers and art prints, I prefer the Liene PixCut S1 to the Cricut StickerPix Print + Cut. The Cricut is a bit cheaper and has its own appeal, but the Liene is the more straightforward, better-rounded tool. It feels like something you can keep on your desk and actually use quickly, rather than another craft machine that needs a bit of planning every time you want to make something.

10 Signs You Might Not Really Be in Love: How to Tell the Difference

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that love can feel like navigating a choose-your-own-adventure book with half the pages missing.
  • Recent findings suggest that wondering how to tell the difference?
  • Recent findings suggest that feeling a bit puzzled about your feelings for boo?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that love can feel like navigating a choose-your-own-adventure book with half the pages missing. Are you truly in love or just caught in a wave of infatuation? Sometimes, what seems like a heart-thumping romance may be a fleeting crush.

Recent findings suggest that wondering how to tell the difference? We’ve got you! Here’s a rundown of the 10 signs you’re not really in love.

Recent findings suggest that feeling a bit puzzled about your feelings for boo? That’s pretty normal. But before you start planning your future or picking out matching Halloween costumes, you may wanna make sure it’s real love and not a case of a serious crush.

Here are some signs that you may not really be in love:.

Industry observers note that caught up in the romance novel vibe? If you’re all about the feelings of being in love rather than who’s sharing your popcorn, it might just be that you’re smitten with the idea of love itself.

Time to check if your relationship is more about the fairy tale than the real person.

Chatting with your partner shouldn’t feel as shallow as a kiddie pool. If deep talks are tougher than pulling teeth and rarer than a unicorn, it’s a red flag.

Sticking to small talk about the weather and dinner intends suggests the emotional depth for a lasting bond might be missing.

When discussions about future aims feel as far-fetched as sci-fi adventures, they may reveal underlying doubts about the relationship’s viability.

In a recent development, if imagining a future together feels unrealistic or undesirable, it’s time to ask yourself why. Real love plans a future; infatuation lives for the weekend.

According to recent reports, remember when their sock on the floor was cute? If little quirks now make you more cranky than charmed, it might mean the love goggles are off, your feelings have shifted from affection to annoyance, and the reality check has bounced.

Love is seeing imperfections and adoring them anyway.

In a recent development, feeling more at ease or more ‘yourself’ when your partner isn’t around is a telling sign. If you’re secretly throwing mini-parties when they leave the room, you need to stop and think. Real-deal love means missing their chaos when they’re gone, not celebrating the silence.

Shared values are the anchor of deep, lasting relationships. If your core values clash more than a polka dot and stripes ensemble, you’re in for a rough ride, as finding common ground could be challenging!

Lasting love grows from shared beliefs and mutual respect, not from opposing battle lines.

According to recent reports, no respect? No future. Respect is as critical to love as air is to breathing. Without mutual respect, you might just be coexisting rather than genuinely connecting.

If you no longer admire or respect each other’s opinions and choices, sustaining a healthy relationship will be difficult.

According to recent reports, if they’re out of sight and totally out of mind, that’s not just independence — it might be indifference. When love is real, you should long for their laugh or lame jokes when they’re away. Could it be that your emotional attachment isn’t as strong as it should be for a lasting relationship?

Industry observers note that if your best moments are consistently away from your partner, your heart might not be in it to win it. Perhaps your relationship isn’t providing enough support or happiness.

Sources indicate that true love enriches your life and doesn’t play second fiddle to your social circle. It’s time to evaluate where your emotional energy is invested.

Recent findings suggest that still window shopping while you’re supposedly locked down? It’s a sign you might not be all in. A love that lasts doesn’t keep a backup catalog — it’s too busy loving what it already has.

Knowing why you’re still scanning for alternatives can help you address what might be missing or unfulfilled in your relationship.

Are you genuinely in love or just in love with being in love? If you’re secretly thrilled when they’re not around, stuck in surface-level chit-chat, or dreading deep-future talks, these are cosmic signs that it’s rethink o’clock.

Don’t ignore the signals — tuning in now can save you heartache later and lead you toward a love that genuinely fulfills you.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that and so, after 13 years and 13 million memes, GTA 6 is finally here.
  • Industry observers note that mike Craddock, CEO and founder of NewGen, has some thoughts.
  • In a recent development, "The main thing for Rockstar won’t be living up to the initial hype, so much as maintaining momentum after the excitement dies down," Craddock tells Creative Bloq.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that and so, after 13 years and 13 million memes, GTA 6 is finally here. And as our reviewer put it, 'Holy sh*t it's good'. But now that the years (and years) of anticipation are over, and the game is finally in players' hands, the question for Rockstar is: what next? Will the hype machine slow down? Or like GTA 5 before it, will the game prove to have a life that extends long beyond the launch date?

Industry observers note that mike Craddock, CEO and founder of NewGen, has some thoughts. Before founding the social creator agency, he built a successful career as a professional YouTuber and Call of Duty player, so he knows a thing or two about what makes a strong legacy for a game.

In a recent development, "The main thing for Rockstar won’t be living up to the initial hype, so much as maintaining momentum after the excitement dies down," Craddock tells Creative Bloq. "GTA is more than a game – it’s been shaping culture for decades. So, with GTA VI, Rockstar has an opportunity to continue to tap into the zeitgeist. And a big part of that opportunity sits with creators. After all, we’ve already seen how roleplay servers have transformed the game into full-blown experiences, building their own characters and storylines. Player-driven worlds have evolved into independent communities across Twitch, Youtube and Tiktok.".

And much like with GTA 5, Craddock believes the world of GTA Online could be the key to GTA 6's longevity. "The further potential for UGC and creator-build mini worlds is massive. In fact, these experiences could become more culturally significant than the original game itself. For Rockstar, that means thinking beyond its post-launch marketing. To move with the times, it needs to give creators the freedom and support to build within the GTA universe – and crucially, not try to control every conversation.".

In a recent development, right now, there is no official word on when, or if, GTA 6 online will arrive. But one thing's for sure – it would lead to a huge wave of user-generated content in the world of Leonida. And as Craddock says, "The measure of GTA VI’s success won’t just be from its launch. It’ll be how it affects pop culture in the years to come.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, lonnie G. Bunch III, the outgoing leader of the Smithsonian Institution, sent a letter to staff on Tuesday (24 November) in an attempt to quell fears of a political takeover after photos leaked of a Trump aide working on an overhaul plan while riding the city's metro.

“The intended use of this list is unclear,” Bunch wrote of “The Smithsonian Institution Renewal Plan” that the staffer was seen editing on his laptop on a crowded train in late October. “What remains clear is that the Smithsonian is an independent institution with the responsibility and privilege to present accurate information to millions of visitors through our scholarship and educational programmes.”.

Photos of the staffer working on the blueprint—in full view of fellow passengers on public transit—had been published by ProPublica the previous day (23 November). Formatted as a 25-item to-do list, the draft focused largely on the beleaguered National Museum of American History (NMAH), a recent focal point in the White House’s attempts to rewrite US history.

Sources indicate that the list included firing NMAH’s director and a dozen other administrators and curators, opening a newly introduced permanent exhibition centred on “Western civilisation inheritance”, erecting a new “colossus statue” of George Washington for NMAH’s entrance and overhauling its online curriculum for schoolchildren to “realign educational materials with patriotism, not ideology”. The strategy also called for a review of Smithsonian grants to “woke third parties” like the American Alliance of Museums.

The Washington Metro’s Smithsonian station Photo: GeneralPunger, via Wikimedia Commons.

Sources indicate that given that it was in process prior to the midterm elections—which resulted in a landslide for Democrats, who gained a majority in both houses of congress—it remains unclear if this plan for the Smithsonian is still in the works. However, congressional Democrats are ready to fight.

“I intend to investigate these matters in the 120th congress and vigorously defend the Smithsonian’s independence,” Chellie Pingree, the ranking member of the congressional subcommittee that funds the Smithsonian, wrote in a letter to the institution’s Board of Regents after the ProPublica leak. “This reporting is extremely concerning, but not surprising given this administration’s previous attempts to illegally impound Smithsonian Institution-appropriated funding, use federal agencies to spread misinformation about the Smithsonian, and release a demonstrably false report accusing the Smithsonian Institution of systemic bias in its curatorial decisions.”.

US President Donald Trump has been steadily attacking the Smithsonian ever since he took office for his second term, with a goal of realigning the institution to complement his own political agenda. Last year, Trump attempted to fire the director of the National Portrait Gallery, Kim Sajet, over her support for diversity, equity and inclusion programmes. She later resigned and now heads the Milwaukee Art Museum in Wisconsin.

Recent findings suggest that in July, NMAH director Anthea M. Hartig was summoned to appear before congress and interrogated by Republican lawmakers after a White House report concluded the museum was not “proudly patriotic” with leadership having “denigrated and displaced whites, males, Christians and Americans”. A few days later, Trump ordered that signs be placed outside the NMAH, warning visitors of "ideological capture" and "inaccurate information" inside. (The signs have yet to be erected.).

Breaking: Say What? 7 Tips to Unclog Your Blocked Ears

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that earwax buildup, allergies, infections, or changes in air pressure might be behind your clogged ears.
  • Whether it’s from a cold, allergies, or changes in air pressure, blocked ears can disrupt your day-to-day activities and even cause discomfort.
  • Clogging can happen either on the inside or the outside of your eardrum.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that earwax buildup, allergies, infections, or changes in air pressure might be behind your clogged ears. There are many easy ways to get relief at home. Whether it’s from a cold, allergies, or changes in air pressure, blocked ears can disrupt your day-to-day activities and even cause discomfort. Thankfully, there are several effective methods to help unclog your ears and restore your hearing. Listen up! Why are my ears clogged? Clogging can happen either on the inside or the outside of your eardrum. Here are the most common ways your ears can get blocked: Earwax in the outer ear helps prevent particles and excess water from entering the middle ear. However, if earwax builds up too much outside the eardrum, it can cause a blockage. If you’ve been swimming recently, some water might be stuck in your ear canal, pushing against your eardrum. When that water hangs around too long, it can lead to a swimmer’s ear, an outer ear infection. Sinus infections, ear infections, and Eustachian tube dysfunction can pressure your eardrum’s inner side. Allergies can cause uncomfortable inflammation and congestion in your ears. Your sinuses, throat, and ears are connected, so when you feel stuffed up and sniffly, your inner ear feels the pain too. Changes in air pressure, like when you fly, can cause uncomfortable ear pressure. Best clogged ear remedies 1. Pop and unclog The easiest way to unclog your ears is by “popping” them. Just pinch your nose shut, seal your lips, and gently blow. This simple technique, known as the Valsalva maneuver, won’t clear earwax or fluid but is a common trick people use on planes. 2. Swallow, yawn, or chew The Eustachian tubes connect your middle ear to the back of your throat. They briefly open when you swallow, yawn, or chew. Altitude changes can cause these tubes to close, but chewing gum or yawning can help reopen them. Alternatively, you can try the Toynbee maneuver, where you hold your nose and swallow. 3. Ear drops Over-the-counter (OTC) ear drops can soften and dissolve excess earwax. If you prefer a DIY approach, warm a small amount of mineral oil and use an eye dropper to apply a few drops into your ear for a few minutes. Pro tip: Baby oil or olive oil can also be used, but make sure it’s not too hot. Additionally, diluted hydrogen peroxide drops can be helpful. 4. Warmth and gravity To loosen up clogged earwax, use a warm, damp washcloth as a compress. Lie down with the clogged ear facing down against the heated washcloth. Gravity and heat will help the earwax move along more easily. 5. Hit the steam room Steam can help drain sinuses and alleviate pressure in your inner ear. Close the bathroom door, let the hot shower run for a while, and then luxuriate with deep, cleansing breaths. 6. Take allergy medication Because your throat, sinuses, and ears are interconnected, any sickness affecting your sinuses or throat can also impact your ears. Over-the-counter antihistamines, decongestants, or nasal sprays can relieve sniffles, coughs, and ear discomfort. 7. Rinse away the gunk Rinsing your nasal passages with a medication-free saline solution can help reduce congestion and clear out mucus that might be causing ear blockage. You can also consider investing in a nasal irrigation system for more thorough mucus clearing. When to see your doctor Have you been unable to unclog your ears for a few days, or are you experiencing severe pain, fever, dizziness, hearing loss, fluid discharge, or unusual odor? If so, it’s crucial to contact your healthcare provider promptly. These symptoms may indicate an infection that needs medical attention. What not to do when you have clogged ears Cotton swabs: Q-tips and other cotton swabs to remove earwax can push it further into your ear canal, so don’t do it. Candling: Ear candles might seem like a fun party trick, but there’s no science to prove they work, and they’ve been shown to cause injuries. Sprays: Decongestant nasal sprays can be helpful, but using them too long can lead to rebound congestion. Drying solutions: A few drops of rubbing alcohol or a mixture of one part vinegar and one part alcohol can help dry out the ears when you have a swimmer’s ear. However, doing this regularly can lead to irritation. Takeaway Clogged ears are often caused by earwax buildup, allergies, infections, or changes in air pressure. You can use over-the-counter or DIY ear drops, irrigation kits, or warm compresses to unblock your ears. Antihistamines or nasal sprays can also help relieve clogs caused by allergies. PSA: Consult a healthcare provider if your blocked ears are painful or at-home remedies don’t work.

It has two mappable rear buttons, analog triggers with travel locks/stoppers, swappable ABXY face buttons, and a magnetic faceplate. And it costs less than the Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller while still supporting gyro motion controls and up to a 1000Hz polling rate.

Multi-platform compatibility works across Nintendo Switch/Switch 2, PC, and mobile devices via Bluetooth, 2.4GHz wireless dongle, or USB, and it comes with a charging stand (which can house the wireless dongle) and a physical power switch to avoid accidental battery drain.

It has been revealed that the G7 Pro 8K's sticks use 'Mag-Res' technology for greater input precision, an the trigger stops are dual-mode, so you can switch between Hall Effect analog triggers and micro-switch triggers. The former is ideal for racing, the latter for RPGs and hectic shooters.

In addition to the remappable back buttons, there are extra L5 and R5 buttons next to left and right triggers, also remappable. Our reviewer found the 6-axis gyroscope offers good motion control, and the rumble motors are immersive and nuanced rather than thunderous and distracting.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Christie’s has added the UK auction house Dreweatts to its portfolio.

In a statement on Wednesday, Christie’s chief executive Bonnie Brennan noted that the auction house has long admired Dreweatts. “Most importantly, our clients collect across categories and at every price point, and together we have the opportunity to provide them with an even broader and more complete level of service. Both businesses will continue to operate much as they do today, while building on their respective strengths and the significant opportunities we see for future growth,” she said. Related Articles Working Mothers Face Pervasive Discrimination in London Art World, Study Finds Yoshitomo Nara Painting Fetches $15.9 M., Outselling Koons and Richter in Latest York.

Dreweatts specializes in single-owner collections and country house sales, ranging from furniture and works of art, old masters, modern and contemporary art, Asian and European ceramics, modern design, jewelry, silver, luxury accessories, clocks and wine. The auction house was founded in 1759 by Thomas Davis, a cabinetmaker, upholsterer and land agent from Abingdon, Oxfordshire. Dreweatts operates its main salesroom from its country house, Donnington Priory, in Newbury, Berkshire, and also has a showroom in London on Pall Mall.

Sources indicate that henry House, chief executive of Dreweatts, remarked in a statement that under this latest arrangement “we can use the additional advantage of one another’s expertise to better serve our buyers and sellers. Dreweatts has had a parent organization before, which enabled us to grow the business and prosper, and this move is an extension of that model.” He added that the Christie’s acquisition provides certainty for the auction house and that Dreweatts will continue, under his and chairman Will Richards’ stewardship.

Christie’s president of EMEA, Anthea Peers, said that the François Pinault-owned auction house recognized Dreweatts as a “healthy, compatible business to our own and the value it can add to what we do for all of our clients.”.

On November 19, Dreweatts presented its Fine Watches & Luxury Accessories auction that totaled £529,934 with an 89% sell-through rate. The sale included fine watches, designer handbags, writing instruments and luxury objects from Patek Philippe, Cartier, Hermès, Chanel and Montblanc. The top lots were a Lange & Söhne that sold for £49,780 and a Montblanc black porcelain fountain pen that sold for £8,320.

Tangerines are not just tasty — they’re a powerhouse of nutrients. Packed with tangy flavor and vibrant orange color, these citrus delights offer a host of health benefits. From boosting your immune system to rejuvenating your skin, tangerines are nutrient-rich allies for your well-being. Let’s delve into their nutritional profile and discover why they’re a smart addition to your diet.

Tangerines are nutritional powerhouses. Here’s what each of these little champs pack under their orange belts:.

Tangerines are teeny cousins of the orange but with a thinner, easier-to-peel skin. They boast a sweet and juicy flavor and pack a ton of vitamins, particularly vitamin C, as well as minerals like potassium, antioxidants, and dietary fiber.

Industry observers note that these tiny bursts of sunshine have many benefits that can significantly enhance your health. Here’s why you might want to make tangerines a regular part of your diet:.

Tangerines are loaded with vitamin C, turning them into tiny, tasty guardians for your health. This crucial vitamin supercharges your immune system by enhancing the function and effectiveness of white blood cells, which are essential for fighting off pathogens and infections. By improving the activity and response of these cells, vitamin C helps your body combat a wide range of infections more effectively.

Therefore, regular consumption of these mini-oranges satisfies your taste buds and boosts your body’s defense mechanisms — a win-win!

According to recent reports, want that glow? Tangerines have got you covered. They’re high in potassium, a real game-changer for regulating hydration and balancing fluid levels in your skin cells. This essential mineral keeps your skin cells plump and hydrated, warding off pesky, dry, dull patches.

Plus, potassium supports the removal of toxins and wastes, which means clearer, more radiant skin.

Tangerines are also a fantastic source of vitamin A, which strengthens the outer layer of your skin, smoothing out wrinkles and reducing fine lines. Along with vitamin C, it’s a potent antioxidant, protecting your skin from the damaging and aging effects of free radicals.

Are you having tummy troubles? Tangerines can help with a fiber boost that keeps things moving smoothly along your digestive tract.

These zesty little superheroes are your gut’s new best friends. They’re loaded with fiber that bulks up and softens things down there, making your bathroom visits smooth and speedy. This fruity fix helps manage everything from irregular pit stops to those bloated bleurgh days.

Industry observers note that fiber also balances your gut flora, promoting a healthy microbial environment in your intestines. This balance is crucial for optimal digestion, nutrient absorption, and immune function.

So, grab a tangerine to remedy your belly blues next time your gut feels out of whack.

Tangerines are a dynamo when it comes to battling serious health baddies like cancer and heart disease. These little orange wonders are loaded with flavonoids, natural compounds that help with heart health and cancer prevention.

In a recent development, flavonoids help relax the blood vessels, lowering blood pressure levels and reducing the strain on your heart. This helps keep your ticker ticking smoothly and reduces the risk of cardiovascular diseases like heart attacks and strokes.

But wait, there’s more! When it comes to cancer, flavonoids mess with the bad guys — cancer cells — stopping them from multiplying and spreading their nonsense around your body.

According to recent reports, keep your peepers sharp with a dose of vitamin A from tangerines. This essential nutrient and compounds like beta-carotene shield your eyes from age-related challenges and support healthy vision. It plays a key role in creating rhodopsin, a protein in your eyes that allows you to see in low-light conditions.

Munching on tangerines helps keep your night vision in superhero shape and supports overall eye function, keeping your peepers sharp and responsive.

Furthermore, tangerines contain other essential eye health nutrients, like lutein and zeaxanthin. These antioxidants are found in high concentrations in the retina, where they help filter blue light and prevent oxidative damage, further protecting the eyes from conditions like cataracts.

Sure, tangerines are delish and make your taste buds do a happy dance, but they’re also packed with nutrients that can seriously amp up your well-being.

Recent findings suggest that from giving your immune system a high-five to keeping your heart beating like a healthy drum, tangerines are basically wellness wrapped in a bright orange peel. So, go grab one and make it your main squeeze!

Future Value Calculator: How to Project Your Investments

📅 30 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1799 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Choosefi

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • What $10,000 grows to at different rates over 30 years — the rate difference matters more than you think.
  • $10,000 invested for 30 years at 10% annual return.
  • Free calculators, a personalized FI roadmap, and a community of 25K+ on the same journey.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

What's your FI number? Calculate it in 60 seconds.

The one number that changes everything.

What $10,000 grows to at different rates over 30 years — the rate difference matters more than you think.

$10,000 invested for 30 years at 6% annual return.

$10,000 invested for 30 years at 8% annual return.

$10,000 invested for 30 years at 10% annual return.

Free calculators, a personalized FI roadmap, and a community of 25K+ on the same journey.

In a recent development, future value (FV) is the projected worth of an investment at a specific point in the future, based on an assumed rate of growth. It answers the most practical question in investing: "If I invest this money today, what will it be worth in 10, 20, or 30 years?".

Future value calculations rest on compound interest — the principle that your returns earn their own returns over time. Albert Einstein reportedly called compound interest "the eighth wonder of the world," and while the attribution is debatable, the math is not. The difference between simple interest (returns on your original investment only) and compound interest (returns on your investment plus accumulated returns) becomes enormous over long time horizons.

The basic future value formula for a lump sum investment is:.

For example, $10,000 invested at 8% for 20 years:.

FV = $10,000 x (1.08)^20 = $10,000 x 4.661 = $46,610.

The table reveals two critical insights. First, small differences in return rates produce massive differences over long periods — $10,000 at 6% grows to $57,435 over 30 years, while the same amount at 10% grows to $174,494. That 4-percentage-point difference triples the outcome. Second, time is the dominant variable. At 8%, your money doubles roughly every 9 years — so 30 years gives you more than three doublings, turning $10,000 into over $100,000.

Most people do not invest a single lump sum and walk away. They invest regularly — monthly or per paycheck — over decades. The future value of a series of regular contributions uses a different formula called the future value of an annuity:.

FV = PMT x [((1 + r)^n - 1) / r].

Where PMT is the periodic contribution, r is the periodic rate, and n is the total number of periods.

Sources indicate that in practice, you do not need to calculate this by hand. The insight that matters is this: regular contributions are far more powerful than most people realize because each contribution starts its own compounding clock. Your first $500 contribution compounds for the full 30 years, while your 360th contribution (at month 360) compounds for just one month — but together they build wealth that dwarfs a single lump sum.

Recent findings suggest that A person investing $500 per month at 8% for 30 years accumulates $745,180 — from total contributions of only $180,000. That means $565,180, or 76% of the final balance, came from compound returns rather than your own deposits. This is the engine of wealth building.

Sources indicate that every future value calculation should be done twice — once in nominal terms and once in real (inflation-adjusted) terms. The nominal return is the raw number your investments earn. The real return subtracts inflation, showing you what your money will actually buy.

According to recent reports, historically, the S&P 500 has returned roughly 10% nominally and 7% after inflation. The difference matters enormously over long periods:.

That $1.13 million in nominal terms has the purchasing power of roughly $610,000 in today's dollars — still excellent, but nearly half less than the headline number suggests. When planning for FI, always use real returns (6-7%) rather than nominal returns (9-10%) to avoid overestimating what your portfolio will actually support in retirement spending.

The Rule of 72 is the simplest and most useful mental math tool in investing. Divide 72 by your annual rate of return to estimate how many years it takes for your investment to double:.

Industry observers note that this works in reverse too. If you want to know what rate of return you need to double your money in 15 years: 72 / 15 = 4.8%. The Rule of 72 is an approximation — it is most accurate for rates between 5% and 12% — but it is remarkably precise within that range and far faster than pulling out a calculator.

According to recent reports, the FI community uses future value calculations as the backbone of retirement planning. The process works in three steps:.

The table highlights how starting balance and monthly contribution interact. Notice that increasing your monthly contribution from $1,500 to $2,500 (a $1,000 increase) with a $100,000 starting balance cuts 3.5 years off your time to $1 million. This is the savings rate lever in action — the amount you save each month matters more than any other variable you control.

Recent findings suggest that A common question is whether it is better to invest a lump sum now or spread contributions over time (dollar-cost averaging). The math is clear: lump sum investing wins approximately two-thirds of the time because markets trend upward over the long term. However, dollar-cost averaging reduces the psychological risk of investing a large amount right before a downturn and provides a behavioral advantage that keeps many investors on track. For most FI-seekers, the question is academic — you invest each paycheck as it arrives because you do not have a large lump sum sitting on the sidelines.

Industry observers note that ready to unlock a world of free travel? Start with the Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card.

$95 annual fee | Earn 75,000 bonus points.

In a recent development, side hustlers! With the Ink Business Preferred® Credit Card you can earn free travel from your business expenses.

The Capital One Venture Rewards Credit Card can be used to offset almost any travel expense.

Recent findings suggest that when projecting your portfolio growth for retirement planning, use real (inflation-adjusted) returns of 6-7% rather than nominal returns of 9-10%. A $1 million nominal balance in 30 years has the purchasing power of roughly $550,000 in today's dollars at 2% average inflation. Planning with real returns ensures you are targeting a portfolio that can actually support your desired spending level.

Track your actual spending for 3 months and annualize it. Multiply by 25 to get your FI number using the 4% safe withdrawal rate. If you spend $60,000 per year, your FI number is $1,500,000.

Add up all retirement accounts (401k, IRA, Roth IRA, HSA), taxable brokerage accounts, and savings. Exclude home equity and non-liquid assets. This is your starting balance for the future value calculation.

Subtract your monthly spending from your monthly after-tax income. Include employer 401(k) match and any other automatic savings. This is your periodic contribution amount for the future value formula.

In a recent development, use the future value of a lump sum plus annuity formula, or a simple online calculator, to project when your current balance plus monthly contributions will reach your FI number. Use 7% real return (after inflation) for conservative planning.

Test what happens if you increase contributions by $200/month, $500/month, or $1,000/month. Seeing the concrete impact of a savings rate increase — often shaving 2-5 years off your FI timeline — makes the trade-offs tangible and motivating.

Industry observers note that for long-term stock market projections, use 7% for inflation-adjusted (real) returns or 10% for nominal returns based on the S&P 500 historical average. For a more conservative estimate, use 6% real. For bond-heavy portfolios, use 3-4% real. Always specify whether you are using nominal or real returns — mixing them up is one of the most common planning mistakes.

It has been revealed that future value calculations show what WOULD happen if returns were constant every year. In reality, markets fluctuate — you might earn 25% one year and lose 15% the next. Over 20-30 year periods, average returns tend to converge toward historical norms, making future value projections reasonably useful for planning. Treat them as directional estimates, not guarantees.

Future value asks: "What will $10,000 today be worth in 20 years?" Present value asks the reverse: "What is $50,000 in 20 years worth in today's dollars?" They use the same variables but in opposite directions. Present value is useful for evaluating whether a future payout (like a pension or annuity) is worth the cost today.

The Rule of 72 works for any compounding rate, including inflation. At 3% inflation, prices double every 24 years (72 / 3 = 24). This means $50,000 in annual spending today becomes $100,000 in 24 years in nominal terms — your purchasing power is halved if your income stays flat. This is why investing in assets that outpace inflation is essential.

Sources indicate that for FI planning, future value is more intuitive — it tells you what your portfolio will grow to. However, the most practical approach is to calculate future value using real (after-inflation) returns. This effectively gives you a future value stated in today's purchasing power, which is what you actually need to know for spending planning.

In a recent development, in tax-advantaged accounts (401k, IRA, Roth IRA, HSA), your investments compound without tax drag, so the standard future value formula works directly. In taxable accounts, capital gains taxes, dividend taxes, and tax-loss harvesting all affect your real return. A rough adjustment is to reduce your assumed return by 0.5-1.0% for taxable accounts to account for ongoing tax drag.

According to recent reports, future value calculations are the most practical tool in the FI planner's toolkit. They turn abstract concepts like compound growth and savings rate into concrete dollar amounts and specific timelines. The key takeaways are straightforward: use 7% real returns for conservative planning, always account for inflation by using real rather than nominal returns, and remember that your monthly contribution rate has a far larger impact on the outcome than chasing an extra point or two of return. The Rule of 72 gives you instant mental math for any investment decision — how long to double, what rate you need, and how inflation erodes purchasing power. Combined with a clear FI number and a disciplined savings rate, future value projections show you exactly when financial independence becomes reality. Run the numbers, test different scenarios, and let the math motivate you to increase that monthly contribution whenever you can.

#114530. Industry News: Five Questions for Advisors on the November Marquee Sales: Guarantees, Spotty Bidding, and a $190 M. Van Gogh

Industry News: Five Questions for Advisors on the November Marquee Sales: Guarantees, Spotty Bidding, and a $190 M. Van Gogh

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 18 min read (3508 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Artnews
